key_insight: LE-DM reconstructs Eulerian velocity fields from particle tracks while dynamically enforcing moving solid boundaries, making the near-surface flow physically consistent and divergence-free.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable pressure, drag, and load estimation around translating, rotating, or deforming bodies in volumetric PTV without treating the whole domain as fluid.
method: Use a time-dependent signed-distance field to classify open fluid, boundary shell, and solid interior nodes.
Solve reconstruction, incompressibility, regularization, and prescribed surface-velocity constraints together on the masked domain.
Support stationary, moving, multiple, and deforming solids with the same framework using only surface velocity and geometry input.
evidence_signal: Validated on an analytical oscillating sphere, synthetic CFD tracks, and a refractive-index-matched tomographic-PTV rising-sphere experiment, with first-cell error reduced from 14% to 3% of body speed and experimental surface velocity recovered at solver tolerance.
watch_item: Performance depends on an accurate signed-distance field and prescribed surface kinematics; errors in boundary geometry or velocity input may degrade the near-wall reconstruction.
paper_title: Dynamic masking for boundary-aware velocity reconstruction in volumetric particle tracking with moving solids
